Dear Mr. Davis,

I am writing to share my feedback about the "City Heritage" walking tour our group took last Saturday. We booked this tour because your company has a great reputation for offering professional, well-informed guides. As someone who really loves history, I was excited to learn about the old buildings and past of the Downtown district. However, the actual experience did not match the high standards promised in your advertisements.

The main problem during the two-hour walk was that our guide, Arthur, did not seem ready. While he was friendly and polite, he did not know much about the city's real history. A few times, he gave dates and facts that were completely wrong. For example, he said the central library was built in the late 1800s, even though a clear cornerstone showing the year 1742 is right on the building for everyone to see. When another person on the tour politely corrected him about the 1812 fire, he looked confused and admitted he was reading from a new script he had not read properly yet.

Also, the tour was not very educational because it lacked a clear plan. Instead of learning about the early days of the city and how people lived back then, we spent most of our time listening to ghost stories and hearing about local souvenir shops. For a pricey tour meant for people who want to learn serious history, this casual approach was disappointing and felt like a waste of our time.

We paid $85 per person specifically to get information from a trained professional. Instead, we got a tour that lacked basic facts and care. This big difference between what your ads promise and what you actually deliver is really bad for your business.

I want to be clear that Arthur was a nice person, but he was simply not ready for this type of tour. To make things right, I am asking for a 50 percent refund of our money, or a credit we can use for a private tour led by one of your experienced senior guides later this year. I hope your company does well, but your services need to match what you advertise.

I look forward to hearing from you soon about how you plan to fix these issues.

Sincerely,
Sarah Jenkins
